candidates.exact_span: A description of how either the Class A or Class B pathogen reduction requirements are met or whether sewage sludge placed on a surface disposal site is covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether Class A, Class B, or surface-disposal covering applies determines which pathogen-related monitoring and recordkeeping obligations are in effect and how to classify periods without corresponding evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Results of a ground-water monitoring program developed by a qualified ground-water scientist, or a certification by a qualified ground-water scientist may be used to demonstrate that sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit does not contaminate an aquifer.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The choice between a groundwater monitoring program and a scientist certification as acceptable evidence affects which monitoring obligations apply to active sewage sludge units and how missing or partial groundwater evidence should be categorized.

candidates.exact_span: Report YES for liner and leachate collection system at surface disposal site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the permittee operates a surface disposal site to which this reporting item applies affects whether this annual DMR reporting obligation is required and how to treat absent liner/leachate data.

candidates.exact_span: The frequency of monitoring listed in Element 2, Section I.D. which applies to the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which Element 2, Section I.D. monitoring frequency applies to the permittee determines the expected monitoring schedule and whether absent results represent a missing-evidence case or a period when monitoring was not required at that frequency.

TCLP Pass/Fail is a compliance-oriented result that may be compared against an applicable limit or standard; interpretation of whether and when TCLP testing is required affects both limit-evaluation rows and monitoring-obligation applicability.

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg ) in the sludge of PCBs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Reported PCB concentration in mg/Kg is a numeric measurement subject to enforceable limit comparison if a PCB limit applies; interpretation of when PCB reporting is required also affects monitoring-obligation evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: Level of pathogen reduction achieved (C lass A or Class B), unless Vector attraction reduction alternative no. 11 is used.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The Class A versus Class B distinction and the exception when vector attraction reduction alternative no. 11 is used conditionally determine whether pathogen-reduction reporting is required and how to classify missing pathogen-reduction data.

candidates.exact_span: List Alternative used as listed in Section I.C.3.(a. or b.). Alternatives describe how the pathogen reduction requirements are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which Section I.C.3.(a. or b.) alternative applies governs the applicable pathogen-reduction pathway and therefore which monitoring and reporting evidence is expected or excused.

candidates.exact_span: Vector attraction reduction Alternative used as listed in Section I.B.4. h.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The selected vector attraction reduction alternative (including whether alternative no. 11 applies) determines conditional monitoring and reporting obligations and affects classification of missing vector-attraction evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Amount of sludge surface disposed in dry metric tons/year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and how much sludge is surface disposed affects whether surface-disposal-related monitoring and reporting requirements are triggered and whether zero-disposal periods excuse those obligations.

candidates.exact_span: A certification statement that all applicable requirements (specifically listed) have been met, and that the permittee understands that there are significant penalties for false certification including fine and imprisonment (See 503.27(a)(1)(ii) or 503.27(a)(2)(ii) whichever applies to the permittees sludge disposal activities) shall be attached to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether 503.27(a)(1)(ii) or 503.27(a)(2)(ii) applies to the permittee's sludge disposal activities determines which certification form is required on the DMR and how to treat absent or incomplete certification evidence.
